# Applications Open: Autodesk Research Residency 2027 Academic Research Cohort


This year’s academic teams will explore human-centered intelligence for design and make

Autodesk Research invites academic teams to apply for the FY28 Academic Research Cohort to explore this year’s theme: **Human-centered intelligence for design and make** .


The[Autodesk Research Residency Program](https://www.research.autodesk.com/research-areas/residency-program/) connects academic researchers, industry innovators, and Autodesk teams through research, experimentation, and knowledge exchange. Applications close **February 14, 2027** .


[Submit a Research Residency Proposal](https://autode.sk/researchresidencyproposal)


**Exploring** **human-centered intelligence for design and make**


Across design and make, AI-enabled systems need to interpret real-world conditions, account for human experience, and support decisions while preserving people’s judgment and creative agency. We welcome academic perspectives that deepen these areas or help us see useful connections among them.


We’re particularly interested in academic research exploring:


-


How we build a reliable picture of a construction project, even when the information is incomplete, and how we identify what we still need to know


-


How data and evaluation methods help us understand people’s experiences of built spaces and bring those insights into design workflows


-


How creators use generative tools to explore new possibilities while keeping creative direction in their hands


**Relevant backgrounds may include construction data and informatics, digital twins, architecture and the built environment, human factors, cognitive science, human-computer interaction, creative practice, and generative media.** Depending on the research, experience in field data capture, evaluating people’s experience of spaces, animation, motion science, or biomechanics may also be useful. We welcome diverse approaches that advance these areas and create opportunities for exchange with Autodesk researchers.


**What Residents Can Expect**


Residents have the opportunity to connect with Autodesk researchers and fellow academic and industry innovators through curated programming, knowledge exchange, and cross-disciplinary collaboration. Depending on project needs and available capacity, additional support may include Autodesk tools, targeted introductions, Technology Center access, and technical expertise.


We welcome teams interested in both advancing their research and contributing to a collaborative, cross-disciplinary community.


**Applying to the FY28 Academic Research Cohort**


We’re looking for academic teams whose work aligns with our FY28 research focus and who are eager to contribute new perspectives and ideas.


**Research in Action: Highlights from Our 2026 Cohort**


Our inaugural Academic Research Cohort brought together 27 teams from 18 institutions, representing more than 80 students and professors. Their work illustrates the range of research and collaboration supported through the Residency.

**MIT — Advancing Sustainable Construction Through 3D Printing**


Through their Autodesk Research Residency, researchers from MIT’s Center for Advanced Production Technologies are exploring how topology optimization and 3D printing can make concrete construction more material-efficient. Working with Autodesk’s Boston Technology Center, the team fabricated and load-tested a 2.3-meter concrete bridge capable of supporting more than 2,000 pounds. Their findings are informing further exploration of reinforced structures, new materials, and scalable fabrication methods.


Read more:[3D-printed bridge points the way to greener construction](https://news.mit.edu/2026/3d-printed-bridge-points-to-greener-construction-0715)

**Sheridan College – Exploring AI-Assisted Animation**


As part of the Autodesk Research Residency Program, Sheridan College’s Screen Industries Research and Training Centre (SIRT) field-tested[MotionMaker](https://blogs.autodesk.com/media-and-entertainment/2025/06/04/meet-motionmaker/) ‘s Bring Your Own Data framework, using custom motion-capture data to train AI models for stylized animation. Their testing has generated insights into how AI can support creative workflows while preserving artistic control, helping inform Autodesk’s evolving animation capabilities. ****


Watch:[Make Your Own AI Model with Your Own Data: MotionMaker in Maya](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UDv9dHys3rI&t=1s)

**California College of the Arts – Exploring Circular Materials and Design**


Through their Autodesk Research Residency, California College of the Arts’ Architectural Ecologies Lab is developing 3D-printable materials from sawdust and agricultural byproducts, while also testing emerging Autodesk Research AI tools for sustainable building design. The team is working toward larger-scale fabrication demonstrations and collaborating with Autodesk on the 2027 Pioneering Biomaterials symposium.


Learn more:[Pioneering Biomaterials 2027](https://pioneeringbiomaterials.com/)


**The FY28 Academic Research Cohort kicks off in April 2027.** We look forward to learning more about your work!
